text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein says he supports "our Palestinian brethren to the utmost of our abilities and there will be no credibility to the peace process without Jerusalem."
- State sector doctors and engineers threaten work stoppage over pay dispute.

- Prime Minister Kabariti will receive from the parliamentary public liberties committee in the next few days a list of names of detainees (arrested during recent bread riots) who are expected to be pardoned by the government.
- King Hussein says that "what is needed now is the implementation of peace accords...the Washington summit has committed the parties to continue talks until they reach solutions."
- New rules for car driving training companies issued by the interior ministry.
- A draft law on industry being prepared to give priority to the private sector.
- National Cable Company employees threaten work stoppage over pay dispute.
- National Action Front deliberates nominating candidates for the elections to a new speaker of parliament in the next session.
- Guard accused of murder pleads not guilty to murder of 26-year-old woman doctor.
- Royal Jordanian airliner carrying Prime Minister Kabariti and 162 passengers makes an emergency landing in Ireland.
- Police arrest gang in attempt to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of drugs and antiquities to neighbouring countries.
- The award of public tenders is based on criteria of justice and competition, says head of state procurement department.
